summary.name: Raymarched Fractal Landscapes
summary.visualIdentity: Reflective fractal solids emerge from dark fog, evolve into a landscape, and return to sculptural lettering. Coherent reflections, spatial scale, and depth are preserved. Category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics. Provenance: extracted from source xanares-738984, added in the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Poster evidence is a single reference, not full-video verification.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly specified for videos and scenes that need true volumetric depth, reflections, and fractal detail. Suited to dramatic reveals moving from fog-defined solids to a terrain and then a sunset. Flat imagery or SVG would fake the depth, so this style is not suited to flat, purely typographic, or 2D-only briefs. Reading-heavy UI is unspecified.
summary.limitations: The preview (3 s) contains no sculptural lettering; lettering is planned for the full video only and is reported as a limitation. Reflections are single-bounce approximations, not path-traced. Lower internal render resolution softens fine detail. Blender/Cycles and UnrealBloom were considered and rejected. Three.js mesh fractals would need huge geometry, so they are not used. Material colors, transmitted light, and thermal ramps are not verified by the palette check. Exact background hex is an authored fallback, not sampled from the source.
summary.palette: Authored suggestion, used only when no task, brand, or approved palette is supplied. Background token #080A0C (scene field, dark fog color, near-black per poster). Foreground token #F2EEE5 (readable layout foreground). Two base colors only; no gradient enabled. Foreground on background contrast is 17.125:1, meeting the 4.5 normal-text target for opaque captions only. Accents are not specified. Background tokens must not be replaced by accent, glass, page, or subject materials. Backgrounds that are textured, transparent, or changing must be verified in rendered frames. Subject materials must not be recolored to match layout roles.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion is driven by GSAP on a paused, registered timeline. The uEmerge uniform morphs fog density and fractal power. Camera position and target follow an authored path, producing a slow dolly in the preview. The uLandscape uniform blends the SDF toward a domain-repeated terrain via smooth-min. Each frame renders synchronously from uniforms with no accumulation, so out-of-order seeks match. Motion cadence should be smooth and coherent, while deliberate cuts or reading holds are preserved. Interaction behavior for HTML is unspecified; reduced-motion handling is only mentioned for the optional combination.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified in the source. Audio direction guidance is generic: suggest music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence based on the topic, audience, and objective, and honor any user audio requirements first. No fixed genre, tempo, instrument, or voice is assigned. Speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture sync must be verified in the final video. Authorized assets must be sourced separately.
summary.assetRequirements: Three.js fullscreen-quad ShaderMaterial with GLSL raymarching. Required: bounded SDF fractal (Mandelbox/Mandelbulb style, e.g. 8 iterations, max 96 march steps, distance clamp). Offscreen WebGLRenderTarget at about 0.5–0.66 scale with linear upsampling. Sculptural lettering needs a precomputed glyph distance texture extruded via max(d2D, |z|-h). Fonts and assets must be loaded before rendering. Motion references are none. Source files and a key-frame contact sheet are deliverables. Fonts and specific glyph assets are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Keep this style dominant. Optional supporting style: style-099 for continuous camera path, within the primary scene and shared time. Do not import its palette, and preserve the primary background and foreground roles. Avoid competing full-scene treatments, unrelated decorative motion, or replacing the verified background. HTML use requires optional motion with reduced-motion handling. This guidance is authored compatibility, not a prior review.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: Three.js with GLSL ShaderMaterial and offscreen rendering, responsible for geometry, materials, lighting, and fog. Motion engine: GSAP, responsible for uniform and camera tweens, with one owner per property. Render pipeline: HyperFrames by default, with Remotion as a conditional fallback only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, recorded with reason. HyperFrames steps include npx hyperframes check, snapshot --at for key moments, and render --quality delivery --output. Seed randomness and drive all updates from shared composition time. Verify opening, action, transition, and closing frames, plus loop seams, before delivery. Optional chroma.js validates colors and checks contrast on composited frames.
